    #138977. How to spend Christmas alone (and actually enjoy it)

    📅 16 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 9m • 📚 Deep Dive (1842 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Calm ↗ Open Full Page

    How to spend Christmas alone (and actually enjoy it)

    📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1842 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Calm

    ⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The street outside is still, your phone hasn’t buzzed with plans, and the whole day is wide open, with no schedule and no one to check in with.
    • Sources indicate that maybe you’re single, estranged or far from family, working the holiday, grieving, or just not in the mood to celebrate.
    • In a recent development, in fact, there are plenty of ways to make the day your own.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Clinically reviewed by Dr. Chris Mosunic, PhD, RD, MBA.

    It’s Christmas morning. The street outside is still, your phone hasn’t buzzed with plans, and the whole day is wide open, with no schedule and no one to check in with. It might feel like a relief, or it might ache. Sometimes it’s both in the same hour.

    Sources indicate that maybe you’re single, estranged or far from family, working the holiday, grieving, or just not in the mood to celebrate. But no matter why you’re spending Christmas alone, the day can still feel warm and full.

    In a recent development, in fact, there are plenty of ways to make the day your own. Here you’ll find ideas for staying in or going out, plus what to do if it gets hard.

    If you’re spending Christmas on your own, you’re far from the only one. More people live alone than ever, and plenty of people simply prefer a quiet holiday.

    With that in mind, being alone and feeling lonely aren't the same thing. Being alone is a circumstance: no one else is around. Loneliness is a feeling of disconnection, and it can show up at a packed holiday table or an empty house.

    Sources indicate that so what makes time alone feel good rather than lonely? A significant factor may be whether you have a say in how you spend it. In three studies where people reported on their moments throughout the day, time alone felt more positive when people chose it for themselves.

    Recent findings suggest that if you didn’t choose to be alone this Christmas, it’s okay if that stings. What you do with the day is still up to you.

    Whether you’re in the mood for a slow day under a blanket, time out among people, or a bit of both, you don’t owe anyone an explanation for how you spend your day.

    If you’d rather stay in, here are a few ways to make the day at home feel comforting.

    1. Start the morning with meditation or journaling: Settle into a comfortable position and let your eyes close or soften. Tune into your breath and the sensations in your body. When thoughts about the day ahead drift in, notice them, then gently return to your breath. Journaling is another way to check in with how you’re feeling.

    💙 Want some guidance for those few minutes? Settle into the Mornings meditation on Calm.

    In a recent development, 2. Cook or order the meal you really want: Skip the turkey-and-trimmings unless you love them. Go for whatever you're craving, whether that’s a roast for one, pancakes at noon, or your go-to takeout. Choosing food you’re excited about can turn an ordinary meal into a treat.

    💙 Listen to Piano for Rainy Days: Nice & Cozy while you cook.

    According to recent reports, 4. Do a movie marathon on your own terms: You get to choose what you watch, and no one talks through the good parts. Line up your favorite holiday films, or skip the Christmas theme entirely and binge the series you’ve been saving.

    It has been revealed that 5. Get lost in a book or an audiobook: A long, quiet day is a great chance to sink into a story without interruption. If your eyes get tired, switch to an audiobook while you putter around or lie on the couch.

    💙 Discover ten self-love activities to improve your well-being.

    Sources indicate that if you’d like to spend the day out of the house, these ideas include solo outings and activities around other people. Holiday hours often change and volunteer spots fill up, so check details as early as you can..

    6. Spend time somewhere green: Stroll along a park path or trail, or find a bench and settle in for a while. Time in green space has been shown to quiet a busy mind. In one study, adults who walked for 90 minutes in nature reported less rumination (the looping, negative thinking that can feed low moods) than those who walked along a busy road.

    💙 Ready to step outside? Try Calm’s Nature Walk meditation with Dr. Eric López to soak in the sights, sounds, and smells around you.

    According to recent reports, 7. Volunteer for a few hours: Soup kitchens, shelters, and animal rescues often need extra hands on Christmas Day. Volunteering connects you with people who share a purpose, and research suggests performing acts of kindness may boost your well-being.

    💙 Feeling the urge to give back? Tune into the Random Acts of Kindness meditation on Calm to see how small gestures add up.

    It has been revealed that 8. Join a community meal or gathering: Many community centers and local groups host open Christmas meals. It’s a low-pressure way to share the day with others, even if only for a couple of hours.

    Industry observers note that 9. Find somewhere that’s open: Movie theaters, some cafés and restaurants, and hotel lounges often keep holiday hours. Even a little time around other people, strangers included, can bring a touch of connection to your day.

    10. Take a day trip: Head to a nearby town, hike a newly introduced trail, or visit a spot you’ve been meaning to see. A change of scenery can make the day feel like an occasion.

    It has been revealed that there are many ways to make a quiet day feel less lonely, from a quick text to a mindfulness practice. Choose whichever of these appeal to you.

    Send a text, leave a voice note, or call someone you care about. If loved ones are far away, you could:.

    Schedule a call in advance, especially if you’re in different time zones.

    Do an activity together over video, like cooking or watching a movie.

    Ask for a family recipe, make it, and share how it turned out.

    According to recent reports, you can start a tradition on your own. Keep it small and simple, such as a letter to your future self you open next year or a movie you rewatch every December 25.

    💙 Not sure where to start? Explore Redefining Traditions with therapist Kati Morton on Calm.

    If you feel loneliness creeping in, a loving-kindness meditation may help you feel more connected. In one study, people who did a short loving-kindness meditation reported more feelings of social connection toward strangers than those who did a control task.

    💙 Press play on the Loving-Kindness meditation on Calm.

    Give yourself one thing to look forward to after your shift, such as a comfort meal or a call with someone you love. Treat yourself during the day with a good coffee or a walk on your break. You can also celebrate with others on another day, and it’s just as meaningful.

    💙 If you’re still feeling lonely after the holiday, here are seven tips to deal with loneliness.

    Even if you’ve chosen to be alone, Christmas can bring up emotions like sadness, envy, or grief. Here’s how to work through them.

    Other people’s picture-perfect holiday photos can leave you feeling like you’re missing out. Try stepping away from your phone for a few hours. Those posts are a highlight reel, and the rest of their day rarely looks as polished.

    Recent findings suggest that if the feeling lingers, try self-compassion: meeting yourself with the same warmth you’d offer a friend who’s feeling down. In a review of studies, people who practiced self-compassion reported lower anxiety, depression, and stress than people who didn’t. You could tell yourself, “This is hard, but I’m doing my best, and that’s enough.”.

    💙 Practice being a Friend on the Inside with Jeff Warren on Calm.

    In a recent development, if you’re missing someone this Christmas, the day can feel especially tender. You can honor them in subtle ways: cook their favorite dish, light a candle in their memory, or write them a letter. There’s no right way to grieve, so let the day be as quiet or as full as you need.

    It’s okay to keep some distance from family on Christmas if you need to. Calls and replies are optional, and so is explaining your choice. You can mute the group chat for the day if that brings you some peace.

    If someone asks what you’re up to, you could say, “I’m keeping it low-key this year.” Whatever comes up, mixed feelings included, you don’t have to push it aside just because it’s the holidays.

    If your sadness lingers past the holiday, disrupts your sleep or appetite, or leaves you feeling hopeless, talk to a doctor or someone you trust. If you’re in the U.S. and need support right away, call or text 988 to reach the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline. If you’re outside the U.S., findahelpline.com lists free local services.

    Industry observers note that if you’re alone for Christmas, it can help to give the day some structure. Pick one or two things that excite you, such as a comfort meal, a long walk, or a movie, and let the rest of the day unfold naturally. A quick call or text with a loved one can be a nice touch, too.

    It has been revealed that it’s normal to want to spend Christmas alone. After a long or busy year, a quiet day can be restful, and preferring it doesn’t mean anything is wrong. Plan the day around what appeals to you.

    If you’d rather not stay home on Christmas, there are plenty of places to spend the day. Look for open movie theaters, cafés, and parks nearby, or join a community meal at a local center. You could also volunteer for an organization to meet people while contributing to a cause. Holiday hours vary, so it’s worth confirming before you head out.

    If you’re single on Christmas, the day is yours to spend however you want. You could cook something you love, explore a new spot, or go for a casual meal or movie with friends.

    If you’re feeling sad or lonely on Christmas, let yourself feel those emotions without judgment. Consider reaching out to a loved one, even briefly. A short meditation can also bring some relief. If the sadness feels overwhelming or won’t lift, speak to a doctor or someone you trust.

    It’s okay to skip Christmas altogether. You can treat December 25 as an ordinary day: rest, work, or do something unrelated to the holiday. If the season stirs up grief or stress, stepping back from holiday prepares is one way to look after yourself.

    In a recent development, A solo tradition can be anything that brings you comfort, whether that’s a special breakfast, a journal entry, or a new ornament you pick out every year. A simple tradition is more likely to stick from year to year.

    Mental health is hard. Getting support doesn't have to be. The Calm app puts the tools to feel better in your back pocket, with personalized content to manage stress and anxiety, get better sleep, and feel more present in your life.

    MCA Chicago receives gift of 65 works, most of them by women and artists of colour

    📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (553 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Theartnewspaper

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • A recent gift of 65 works to the Museum of Contemporary Art (MCA) Chicago honours the institution's upcoming 60th anniversary and its outgoing director, Madeleine Grynsztejn.
    • Sources indicate that the philanthropists Jack and Sandy Guthman worked with the MCA’s curatorial team, poring through the couple’s extensive collection to choose the pieces.
    • In a recent development, grynsztejn considers this an extraordinary model for what can happen when a museum and philanthropists are in alignment.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    A recent gift of 65 works to the Museum of Contemporary Art (MCA) Chicago honours the institution's upcoming 60th anniversary and its outgoing director, Madeleine Grynsztejn.

    Sources indicate that the philanthropists Jack and Sandy Guthman worked with the MCA’s curatorial team, poring through the couple’s extensive collection to choose the pieces. Grynsztejn got the selection down to 65, then hit a wall. Paring it down to 60, as originally intended, became an excruciating process. The Guthmans, champions of the MCA for decades, did not force the museum to choose just 60.

    In a recent development, grynsztejn considers this an extraordinary model for what can happen when a museum and philanthropists are in alignment. To date, the Guthmans have donated 130 works to the MCA—the largest donor gift in the museum’s history.

    For Grynsztejn, building a great museum collection takes not only visionary leadership but visionary philanthropy. “The Guthmans have invested in Chicago artists, making their gift one that also has a civic impact,” she tells The Art Newspaper. Included in the gift is work by Amanda Williams, Dawoud Bey and Rashid Johnson.

    The Guthmans have spent decades supporting Chicago’s civic and cultural institutions. As a real estate lawyer, Jack started out by providing pro bono services. Meanwhile, Sandy directed her family’s foundation Polk Bros. Jack was elected as a trustee of the MCA in 1989 and currently serves on its board. For the MCA’s 50th anniversary, the couple donated 50 photographs by women artists.

    Christopher Wool’s Untitled (1995–96) Photo: Nathan Keay, © MCA Chicago.

    It has been revealed that the current gift includes 23 pieces by artists of colour and 19 by women. Thirteen artists are newly introduced to the MCA’s collection, including Mohamed Bourouissa, James Casebere, Julia Fish, Christian Marclay, Adrian Paci, Elle Perez and Shinique Smith. Other gifts, like photographs by Bey, deepen the MCA’s holdings.

    “In some cases, we are adding an entirely fresh collection,” Grynsztejn claims, referring to Bey’s early photography in Harlem, “and in some cases, we are gaining an icon, as in Christopher Wool’s Untitled (1995-96).”.

    The MCA began as a kunsthalle in 1967. It started receiving gifts, so in 1974 it formalised its collection. Despite the fact that the very first piece to enter the MCA’s collection was by Marisol, it eventually began to reflect the usual gender and racial biases.

    Industry observers note that during her tenure, Grynsztejn has sought to change that by establishing the Women Artists Initiative, inspired by the experience of many colleagues who have found it more challenging to fundraise for exhibitions by women artists. The museum’s proof-of-concept came with the success of exhibitions by Faith Ringgold, followed by a traveling Yoko Ono retrospective. The MCA has added women artists to the collection at four times the national average. Recently, the initiative has been renamed the Madeleine Fund for Women Artists and now has a $5m endowment.

    Sources indicate that since Grynsztejn’s arrival at the museum in 2008, the MCA’s collection has grown from approximately 1,300 to 3,800 works. At least half of the acquisitions under her leadership have been by women and artists of colour. “This is not woke or [diversity, equity and inclusion],” she notes. “It’s good business and good culture. Because if you are a public trust, you are in service to your public.”.

    #138971. Skip Potatoes: Make Beef Stew 100% More Delicious With An Ingredient From The Frozen Aisle

    📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (508 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Foodrepublic ↗ Open Full Page

    Skip Potatoes: Make Beef Stew 100% More Delicious With An Ingredient From The Frozen Aisle

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (508 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Foodrepublic

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Sources indicate that potatoes are almost as notable to beef stew as the meat itself.
    • Pierogi are European-style dumplings that you can stuff with everything from chicken to sauerkraut.
    • Sources indicate that this is an especially fantastic trick if you don't have much meat to begin with, bulking up your stew quite inexpensively.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sources indicate that potatoes are almost as notable to beef stew as the meat itself. But when you substitute them with pierogi, you aren't necessarily removing the tuber so much as transforming its shape and making it 100% more delicious with a variety of other fillings.

    Pierogi are European-style dumplings that you can stuff with everything from chicken to sauerkraut. Still, potato-based fillings are by far the most common, thanks to the delicious combination of a tender wrapping and rich, buttery center that freezes quite well. Making a sort of dumpling soup is one of the best ways to upgrade frozen pierogi, suffusing the dough with an incredibly savory beefiness that's almost impossible to replicate. But it also levels up your stew because you're essentially adding little pockets of mashed potatoes that won't dissipate into the broth!

    Sources indicate that this is an especially fantastic trick if you don't have much meat to begin with, bulking up your stew quite inexpensively. It's also a way to add ingredients that may not usually make their way into your recipe. Melting cheese directly into the pot may mess up the texture, but contained quantities of cheesy potatoes taste amazing when paired with an umami- and herb-rich broth. The best frozen pierogi brands also come with plenty of their own seasoning, so while bites of the dumplings will have an intense flavor, they won't overseason your stew directly unless you boil them so long that the wrapping breaks.

    Beef stew typically needs to cook for at least a couple of hours to develop flavors and tenderize the ingredients. If you add pierogi right away, you run the risk of overboiling the dumplings and making them fall apart. Whether you drop them into the pot to let the wrappings absorb flavor or prepare them separately, timing is critical to preserving their texture.

    Recent findings suggest that if you blueprint on adding pierogi directly to the stew, it's best to leave them frozen. This allows the wrapping to absorb flavorful broth as the filling thaws. In a pot already at a simmer, 10 minutes should be all you need to ensure everything is heated through. If you use mini versions instead of full-size ones, you may want to cut this down to five minutes — when in doubt, follow package instructions. You can always add a lid and let the residual heat warm them through, but these are much easier to overcook.

    Pan-frying pierogi first, then using them as a topping, can be a great way to add a more diverse range of flavors. Properly browned dough not only has a great depth of flavor, but also tends to stand up better against liquids and won't become soggy as quickly. This is especially good for leftovers since you can store your stew and dumplings separately so they won't become oversaturated in the fridge. Frying them up in butter can also add a bit of needed fat if you use a particularly lean cut of meat, making your stew richer.

    #138969. Industry News: This Classic Italian Sandwich Is Extra Crispy & Delicious

    📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (594 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Foodrepublic ↗ Open Full Page

    Industry News: This Classic Italian Sandwich Is Extra Crispy & Delicious

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (594 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Foodrepublic

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Everybody celebrates Italy for pizza, pasta, and gelato, and while they're classics for a reason, we implore you to explore Italy's unrivaled gastronomic tapestry a little deeper.
    • In a recent development, porchetta is a style of pork roast, but is completely unique in its preparation.
    • According to recent reports, porchetta is a meal in itself, but goes even better in a sandwich.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Everybody celebrates Italy for pizza, pasta, and gelato, and while they're classics for a reason, we implore you to explore Italy's unrivaled gastronomic tapestry a little deeper. Trust us, there are some serious gems hidden just beneath the surface. One of our favorite Italian street foods that you need to try is porchetta, Italy's answer to crispy pork belly. Irresistibly crunchy and bursting with indulgent flavors, it makes for a seriously delicious sandwich filler.

    In a recent development, porchetta is a style of pork roast, but is completely unique in its preparation. It's typically made from a whole deboned pig or a large cut of pork belly, which is laid flat and heavily rubbed on the inside with salt, garlic, and black pepper, alongside quintessential Italian seasonings like rosemary, sage, and fennel seeds. The pork is then rolled back together and slow-roasted for several hours, allowing the interior to turn soft and tender while the skin develops a beautiful crackling.

    According to recent reports, porchetta is a meal in itself, but goes even better in a sandwich. Start out with a thick Italian white bread, something that won't turn soggy when paired with the pork's rich meat juices and sauces — ciabatta or focaccia work perfectly here. To balance the richness, add something bright with a little zing. We think salsa verde is an excellent choice, since the lemon juice and vinegar bring a sharp acidity, while fresh parsley keeps the heavy roast from feeling cloying — it pairs perfectly with a Cuban interpretation of the recipe as well. Rather than piling on thick slabs of porchetta, slice it thinly, so it stays tender and folds nearly into the bread, and make sure every sandwich gets a few pieces of the crackling skin for a satisfying crunch. As for what else to put on the sandwich, draw inspiration from Bobby Flay's favorite Roman porchetta sandwich.

    You should have no problem finding pre-rolled porchetta at the butcher, but why not save your money and make it at home instead? We promise it's not as intimidating as it looks. For the juiciest cut that's also easiest to roll and inexpensive, pick up a skin-on pork belly. Its exceptionally high fat content keeps the roast moist and makes it incredibly forgiving to work with, so even the least confident cooks won't have to worry about overcooking it.

    In a recent development, porchetta is the star of the sandwich, and it's the crackling skin that really steals the show, so getting it earth-shatteringly crispy is essential. Here, the secret to a crunchy crust is dryness, so before you get to work on seasoning, leave the pork uncovered in the fridge overnight to let the surface dry out. Many cooks also salt the meat generously before its rest, which draws out even more moisture. And before roasting, it's good practice to pat the skin completely dry, since any lingering moisture turns to steam and keeps the skin from crisping.

    In a recent development, to keep the sandwich from turning into a soggy mess, it's essential to let your porchetta rest for around 15 to 30 minutes after roasting. It might be tempting to carve it right away and admire your hard work, but slicing too soon sends the flavorful juices flooding into the chopping board and then straight into the bread, which even the sturdiest ciabatta can't hold back. The logic is the same as with steak because resting gives the juices time to redistribute through the muscle, leaving the meat deliciously tender and flavorful.

    #138965. Make Your Burgers Juicier With One Creamy Ingredient (Hint: It's Not Butter Or Milk)

    📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 2m • 📖 Standard (473 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Foodrepublic ↗ Open Full Page

    Make Your Burgers Juicier With One Creamy Ingredient (Hint: It's Not Butter Or Milk)

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (473 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Foodrepublic

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • There are a million ways to make patties juicier, from mixing in grated butter to even marinating your burgers.
    • While it may sound odd, this recipe is actually a variation of a Juicy Lucy cheeseburger, a Minnesota staple dating back to the 1950s.
    • While you can always stuff your burgers with other cheeses, Velveeta has one major advantage.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    There are a million ways to make patties juicier, from mixing in grated butter to even marinating your burgers. But if you're looking for something a bit outside the box that doesn't complicate the recipe too much, stuffing the patties with Velveeta can give you some seriously cheesy, moisture-rich results.

    While it may sound odd, this recipe is actually a variation of a Juicy Lucy cheeseburger, a Minnesota staple dating back to the 1950s. The idea is that by trapping Velveeta between two thin patties, the cheese melts into a liquid center that mingles with the rendered meat juices, adding moisture to every bite. If done correctly, the cheese should settle back into a gooey state while the patties rest, helping ensure that you don't burn your mouth on molten dairy on your first bite.

    While you can always stuff your burgers with other cheeses, Velveeta has one major advantage. Thanks to its emulsifying and stabilizing agents, it's less likely to become greasy as it melts. Other meltable cheeses can release fat as they heat up, which isn't a problem when it can drip onto a grill but can create problems when you leave it no room to escape. Plus, the fact that Velveeta comes in blocks makes it extremely easy to shape to fit your patties, no matter how large or small you prefer them.

    The classic Juicy Lucy burger may seem a little daunting, but the process is actually quite simple. Trapping the cheese between the patties and ensuring that all your ingredients and, more importantly, your grill are at the right temperatures are all you really need to worry about for something crisp, delicious, and juicy.

    Starting with one part Velveeta to four parts beef is your best bet for this recipe. It's enough cheese to achieve that gooey center but not so much that it'll escape and ruin the integrity of your patties. It's also best to keep your patties flat rather than thick, which makes it much easier to pinch the seams and trap the Velveeta between them. Velveeta is easier to work with when cold, but keeping your beef cold is also a major benefit for your burger. Cold beef fat is less likely to smear and instead stays in little pockets that help keep the meat even juicier.

    Grilling your burgers at the right temperature helps you achieve a good crust without excessive moisture loss, and it's doubly vital when you stuff the patties. You want enough heat to char the exterior but not so much that the patties finish cooking before your Velveeta has the chance to melt. Around 400 degrees Fahrenheit is a good sweet spot. It may be useful to keep one side of your grill cool, letting indirect heat finish any patties whose exteriors have cooked too promptly.

    Give Your McDonald's Egg McMuffin Double The Flavor With A Twist Workers Love

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (488 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Foodrepublic

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It has been revealed that mcDonald's Egg McMuffin is an iconic sandwich within the fast food breakfast realm.
    • Tristen Epps-Long, Season 22 winner of Bravo's "Top Chef" and a former McDonald's chef, shared this savory-sweet Mickey D's menu hack in an exclusive interview with Food Republic.
    • In a recent development, executing this McMuffin double-down is easy to do.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that mcDonald's Egg McMuffin is an iconic sandwich within the fast food breakfast realm. The chain took the McMuffin from good to great when its restaurants began toasting the English muffin halves in real butter rather than margarine. Customers have also found their own methods for upgrading this legendary breakfast sandwich, such as adding hash brown patties into the mix or giving it a flavor twist with sweet add-ons. The latter practice actually harks back to the 1970s, when the sandwich was served with sugary condiments like honey and jam. While that didn't last long as a standard practice, you can still DIY your own sweet toppings to get twice the eating pleasure out of just one Egg McMuffin.

    Tristen Epps-Long, Season 22 winner of Bravo's "Top Chef" and a former McDonald's chef, shared this savory-sweet Mickey D's menu hack in an exclusive interview with Food Republic. "I like to take my sandwich apart a little bit, so half of it becomes jellied and buttered and the other half of it becomes open-faced and savory," the expert shared.

    In a recent development, executing this McMuffin double-down is easy to do. Simply remove the sandwich's top English muffin half, exposing the Canadian bacon, egg, and cheese below. This provides the open-faced, savory portion to enjoy — nothing more to do. On the other muffin slice, apply your choice of the Strawberry Preserves or Grape Jam commonly offered at McD's restaurants (or you can combine the two to give your spread a mixed berry vibe). Voila! You have something satisfyingly sweet to crown your McMuffin feasting.

    It has been revealed that when sweet meets salty, the resulting flavor wizardry is deeply satisfying. There are various other ways to apply this savory-sweet magic and take your McDonald's Egg McMuffin to the next level. Maple-flavored bacon is a popular breakfast staple, and you can bring that vibe to your McMuffin by pouring McDonald's Hotcake Syrup over the sandwich's Canadian bacon and letting it drip over the other elements. The maple-flavored sweetness brings a delightful dimension to the classic sandwich that is lip-smackingly scrumptious and the perfect foil for its salty heartiness.

    Adding a packet of Mickey D's honey is another sweetening twist that gives your McMuffin honey ham flair. The honey is actually offered as a dipping sauce option for Chicken McNuggets, but no diehard Golden Arches diner will let that stop them from drizzling it onto a McMuffin for added sweetness.

    McDonald's also frequently releases promotional, limited-time sauces, many of which hit those sweet-savory notes with aplomb. Options like Hot Honey Sauce and spicy-sweet Hunter Sauce were among limited-time options that dropped in 2026. You don't have to strictly wait for a limited-edition sauce, though — Mickey D's Sweet 'N Sour Sauce and Creamy Chili McCrispy Strip Dip are on offer year-round to lend sweetness and other flavor dimensions to your Egg McMuffin.

    #138958. Panic attack hangover: 12 ways to recover and feel better

    📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 13m • 📚 Deep Dive (2539 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚠️ Warning 🌐 Calm ↗ Open Full Page

    Panic attack hangover: 12 ways to recover and feel better

    📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 13 min read (2539 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Calm

    ⏱️ ~13 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, you’re finally on the other side of the panic attack.
    • Industry observers note that the hours (or even days) after a panic episode can feel foggy and disorienting.
    • Understanding what’s happening can ease some of the worry, and having a few gentle tools on hand can make the aftermath feel a little less isolating.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Clinically reviewed by Dr. Chris Mosunic, PhD, RD, MBA.

    According to recent reports, you’re finally on the other side of the panic attack. The chest tightness has eased, the shaking has stopped, and your breathing feels more steady. But instead of relief, there’s a strange exhaustion settling in, like you just ran a marathon you don’t remember signing up for. This is often called a panic attack hangover.

    Industry observers note that the hours (or even days) after a panic episode can feel foggy and disorienting. You might experience headaches, sore muscles, difficulty concentrating, or an overwhelming need to crash. These symptoms can feel alarming if no one ever mentioned they might show up, but they’re actually a normal part of the body’s recovery process.

    Understanding what’s happening can ease some of the worry, and having a few gentle tools on hand can make the aftermath feel a little less isolating. Here’s what to know about panic attack hangovers, along with research-backed tips to support yourself through them.

    According to recent reports, A panic attack hangover is the period of lingering after-effects that follow a panic attack. Even though the rush of fear and physical symptoms has eased, your body can still feel off-balance for hours or even days afterward. Many people describe it as feeling strangely similar to an alcohol hangover: foggy, heavy, and emotionally sensitive.

    The experience can be unsettling, especially if you didn’t expect panic to have an “aftermath.” But panic attack hangovers are both common and temporary. They’re simply your body’s way of recovering from an intense stress response.

    Recent findings suggest that note: This guide focuses on panic attacks. If you’ve had an anxiety attack, which builds more gradually, read How to manage symptoms and find ease after an anxiety attack instead.

    While panic attack hangovers can happen at any time, the effects aren’t the same for everyone. Still, there are some common symptoms people notice after a panic attack, some more frequently than others.

    Fatigue or exhaustion: You might feel like your body’s battery has been completely drained.

    Brain fog: You could find it hard to focus, remember things, or think clearly.

    Muscle tension or soreness: Your jaw, shoulders, or chest might feel tight, achy, or tender from holding too much stress.

    Emotional sensitivity: You may notice yourself crying more easily or feeling unusually fragile in everyday situations.

    Headaches: You might experience pressure or pain often triggered by stress, shallow breathing, or unconscious clenching.

    Digestive complications: You could have nausea, stomach discomfort, or sudden changes in your appetite that don’t seem to track.

    Sleepiness or difficulty sleeping: You may find yourself crashing hard into deep rest or lying awake because you’re unable to settle down.

    Sources indicate that these symptoms usually fade within a day, although they can last longer depending on the amount of sleep you get, your stress levels, and your overall health. If they’re frequent or overwhelming, though, it may be a sign to get additional support.

    Industry observers note that the reason panic leaves a hangover comes down to how your body handles stress. A panic attack sends your nervous system into full alert: your heart races, your breath quickens, and your muscles tighten. This is an ancient survival mechanism that’s been designed to keep you safe in an emergency.

    Sources indicate that the problem? Even when the threat isn’t real, your body still goes through the motions without an outlet to use up that surge of energy.

    Sources indicate that once the attack ends, your system shifts into recovery mode. That crash can leave you feeling shaky, sore, and depleted… much like finishing an intense workout. On top of that, the emotional weight of the experience—fear, vulnerability, or the worry it might happen again—can keep your brain buzzing even while your body’s trying to rest.

    This combination of physical exhaustion and emotional strain creates the foggy, heavy state that many people call a panic attack hangover.

    Recent findings suggest that related read: Panic attack vs. anxiety attack? Here's the difference.

    According to recent reports, panic attack hangovers can hit you hard, and you may not have the energy to do much after. These ideas are simple, low-lift, and designed for the days when everything feels like just too much.

    Pick what’s doable today and ignore the rest: your nervous system will get the memo.

    Your body just ran an internal marathon, and it’s notable to be kind to it. If you can, postpone non-urgent tasks and try to give yourself a small recovery window.

    Set a 10–15 minute timer, lie down or sit with support behind your back, and let your eyes rest. If you’re at work, try a short break, plus two minutes of slow breathing in a quiet corner. A pause can often help you recover faster.

    Related read: Stressed and short on time? Here's how to try micro-meditation.

    Staying hydrated and keeping your blood sugar steady can help you feel more balanced as your body recovers from a panic attack. Dehydration and dips in blood sugar can make fatigue, headaches, and brain fog worse.

    It has been revealed that drink water or an electrolyte beverage and have a simple snack, like fruit with nut butter, yogurt, or toast. This helps give your system some fuel to reset.

    Industry observers note that slow, gentle breathing tells your nervous system that you’re safe. Try this for 2–3 minutes: Inhale through your nose for four counts, and then exhale through pursed lips for six or eight.

    Longer exhales can help your nervous system shift from fight-or-flight into rest-and-digest mode. But only do this if you feel comfortable. Don’t try to force anything.

    💙 If you need some guidance, check out Reset with the Breath with Jay Shetty on the Calm app.

    Panic can cause you to tighten your muscles, especially in the jaw, chest, shoulders, and hands. Short, light movements help clear it all without overexertion.

    According to recent reports, you don’t have to do anything too intense. Simple shoulder rolls, gentle neck circles, a slow doorframe chest stretch, or a five-minute walk around the block or office floor can all help. If you’re seated, simply unclench your jaw, open and close your hands 10 times, or shake out your arms. The point is to loosen everything up.

    It has been revealed that 💙 Need a little extra support? Try the Softening Anxiety Daily Move session with Mel Mah on the Calm app.

    Quick temperature shifts, like splashing cool water on your face or holding something cold, can help ground you and interrupt the leftover jitters after a panic attack.

    This is because it’s actually a form of grounding that allows your nervous system to anchor itself back to the present moment.

    Related read: 18 grounding techniques to help relieve anxiety.

    Decision fatigue amplifies the brain fog that comes after a panic attack, so try to cut down on the number of choices you’re making.

    Trim your to-do list to one or two essentials, and choose “good enough” over perfect. Reheat leftovers instead of cooking, tell your coworkers you’re running a little behind, and move all noncritical tasks to the next day. It sounds simple, but having that space will help more than you know.

    Sources indicate that reduce stimulation to ease the post-panic attack stress. Dim overhead lights, switch to warm lamps, lower the volume on any music or background noise, and silence non-urgent notifications on your phone and laptop for an hour.

    If noise is unavoidable, try earplugs or a brown-noise playlist. If you enjoy aromatherapy a familiar scent (like lavender, vanilla, or eucalyptus) can also be grounding.

    Sources indicate that writing a few lines about your feelings and symptoms post-panic attack can help your brain process what happened and move forward. Research reveals that journaling supports emotional regulation, which is why so many people find it useful for panic recovery, too — even if it’s just a quick note or voice memo.

    Consider reflecting on what triggered your attack, what symptoms you noticed, what helped calm you down, and what you could do differently next time. This can help give you more effective coping tools for future attacks.

    Reaching out, even with a simple text, helps calm the nervous system. Social support is one of the strongest buffers for stress recovery.

    Send a text to someone you trust, simply asking to check in. If talking feels like too much, having someone just sit with you can also be helpful.

    Related read: How to help someone having a panic attack (and what to avoid).

    After a panic attack, your system is more sensitive. Consider skipping or reducing how much caffeine you drink, as it can re-spark jitters. And avoid alcohol, as it’s been known to disrupt sleep and mood. Swap in decaf, herbal tea, or a half-caf and make sure to focus on nutrition and hydration to help support recovery.

    Sources indicate that fatigue after a panic attack is real, and quality sleep helps reset your stress response. Keep bedtime predictable with a wind-down routine you enjoy, darken the room, and cool it slightly.

    If you desperately need a nap, cap it at 20–30 minutes, and avoid late-evening naps in order to protect nighttime sleep. If your mind spins when it’s time to go to bed, try a quiet meditation or body scan. This can help quiet the mind long enough to help you drift off faster.

    💙 Fall asleep with ease thanks to the White Noise soundscape on the Calm app.

    Industry observers note that even just knowing what you’ll do next time can take the edge off that heavy, shaky feeling that lingers after a panic attack. One simple idea? Make a three-step proposal that you keep on your phone or in your wallet.

    Spend two minutes on long exhales or humming.

    Splash cold water on your face or run cool water over your wrists.

    It also helps to add one contact you trust to call or text.

    While you may not be able to prevent every spiral, it always helps to have something in your back pocket (literally) that helps you feel less alone and more ready.

    Yes, a hangover can sometimes trigger panic attacks. This is because alcohol disrupts sleep, dehydrates your body, and causes blood sugar swings — and all of these effects can make your nervous system more sensitive the next day.

    Alcohol also interferes with the neurotransmitters that regulate your mood, which can amplify feelings of unease or dread. If you’re already prone to anxiety, that extra stress can tip into panic.

    Every person who drinks won’t necessarily have a panic attack, but if you notice a pattern between hangovers and panic, it may help to cut back, hydrate more intentionally, or avoid drinking on nights before demanding days.

    For most people, the hungover feeling eases within a few hours, but it’s not unusual for fatigue or brain fog to stretch into the next day. The duration of a panic attack hangover depends on several factors: how intense the panic attack was, how long it lasted, how well you slept, and what kind of support you gave your body afterward.

    Industry observers note that try to find the recovery initiative that works best for you: getting enough water, food, gentle movement, and rest can speed up the reset. However, if you find that your hangover lasts longer than 24 hours or happens every time you panic, it may be a sign that your nervous system is under strain. In this case, getting some professional support can help.

    Brain fog and fatigue are your nervous system’s way of asking for recovery time, so supporting your body can make the fog lift faster. Start with water or an electrolyte drink, followed by a small, balanced meal or snack. Light movement like walking or stretching also helps by boosting circulation and clearing leftover stress hormones, while short breaks from screens give your brain a reset.

    Sources indicate that some people find that changing environments—stepping outside for fresh air, moving to a quieter space, or dimming harsh lighting—makes a noticeable difference in clarity. Rest is notable, too, but you don’t want to overdo it. A short nap capped at 20–30 minutes usually helps more than staying in bed for hours.

    Sources indicate that the exhaustion you feel after a panic attack is the crash that comes after an adrenaline surge. Basically, when you panic, your body burns through enormous amounts of energy in a short time. Your heart rate rises, your muscles tense, and your brain goes into overdrive to scan for danger.

    It has been revealed that even though there isn’t an actual threat, your body doesn’t know that, so it uses up its resources as if there is. Once the panic attack passes, your hormones shift, and your body needs to come down from the emotional intensity. While it’s easy to look at this exhaustion as weakness, it’s really just your body’s way of recovering from an all-systems-on alert. That’s why gentleness is key for recovery.

    You can’t always prevent panic attacks, but you can definitely soften the after-effects. The most helpful strategies are proactive, or preventing one before it comes on. Think: getting consistent sleep, eating balanced meals to keep blood sugar steady, staying hydrated, and limiting alcohol or excessive caffeine.

    Industry observers note that some people find it useful to have a short aftercare routine ready, too, such as hydrating, stretching, or texting a friend once the panic subsides. This helps to prevent the hangover from stretching out longer than necessary.

    In a recent development, over time, therapy and skills training can also reduce both the frequency of panic attacks and the severity of hangovers. You’ll essentially learn how to give your nervous system a softer landing.

    Headaches and sore muscles are common after a panic attack. During panic, your jaw, neck, shoulders, and chest may tighten without you noticing, and fast, shallow breathing could add to the headache.

    Unclenching your jaw, rolling your shoulders, or holding a cool compress to your forehead may help. Get care right away if you have a sudden, severe headache, chest pain, numbness or weakness, trouble speaking, or vision changes. If your headache lasts longer than you’d expect, check in with your doctor or primary care provider.

    After a panic attack, give your body a few minutes to settle before you do anything else. Stay where you are if it’s safe, and take a few slow breaths with a longer exhale.

    In a recent development, shakiness or fog is a normal part of coming down from panic, so you don’t need to push through it. Once the first wave passes, tell someone you trust what happened and lower the demands on yourself for the rest of the day. The 12 tips above have ideas for the hours that follow. If panic attacks keep happening, talking with a doctor or mental health professional may help.

    Industry observers note that mental health is hard. Getting support doesn't have to be. The Calm app puts the tools to feel better in your back pocket, with personalized content to manage stress and anxiety, get better sleep, and feel more present in your life.

    Two Everyday Drink Swaps Are Linked To Less Weight Gain

    📅 11 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (472 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Org

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Swapping just three drinks a week was linked to less weight gain over four years.
    • In a recent development, swapping just three drinks a week was linked to less weight gain over four years.
    • Swapping sugary drinks for water is linked to less weight gain over time, according to a study of more than 140,000 adults.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Swapping just three drinks a week was linked to less weight gain over four years. What mattered was which drinks people gave up.

    In a recent development, swapping just three drinks a week was linked to less weight gain over four years. What mattered was which drinks people gave up.

    Swapping sugary drinks for water is linked to less weight gain over time, according to a study of more than 140,000 adults.

    Replacing them with diet drinks reveals much the same pattern.

    Switching from diet drinks to water was linked to a much smaller difference in weight.

    Both swaps could make a difference by cutting the calories people get from their usual soft drinks.

    A diet version can also preserve the familiar sweet taste, which may make the change easier for some people to stick with.

    The findings suggest that the drink someone gives up may matter more for their weight than which of these two alternatives they choose.

    The researchers drew on three long-running US studies that followed nurses and other health professionals for a typical period of 28 years.

    Participants regularly reported what they drank and how much they weighed, allowing researchers to see how their drinking habits and weight shifted over four-year periods.

    The researchers estimated about 1.4 kg less weight gain over four years when three sugary drinks a week were replaced with either water or diet drinks.

    The estimated difference for replacing three diet drinks a week with water was only about a tenth of a kilogram over the same period.

    People who cut back on sugary drinks tended to gain less weight whether or not they increased their intake of diet drinks.

    The researchers estimated the swaps from changes in people’s reported habits, so the study can show associations but cannot establish how much weight any individual would gain or lose after making the switch.

    Replacing a regular soft drink with its diet version changes the calories while keeping much of the experience of having a sweet drink.

    Switching to water also removes the sweet taste, which may change how much sweetness people prefer over time.

    In a separate year-long randomised trial, people assigned to replace sugary drinks with unsweetened ones indicated a greater drop in their preferred level of sweetness than those assigned to artificially sweetened drinks (Ebbeling et al., 2020).

    That change in taste preference offers a possible reason why an unsweetened choice might become more appealing with time.

    The study was published in the American Journal of Clinical Nutrition (Espinosa et al., 2026).

    Psychologist, Jeremy Dean, PhD is the founder and author of PsyBlog. He holds a doctorate in psychology from University College London and two other advanced degrees in psychology. He has been writing about scientific research on PsyBlog since 2004. View all posts by Dr Jeremy Dean.

    #138956. Not Butter, Oil, Or Lard: Chicken Skin Is 10x Crispier With This Rich Ingredient

    Not Butter, Oil, Or Lard: Chicken Skin Is 10x Crispier With This Rich Ingredient

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (403 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Foodrepublic

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Top-notch crispy chicken skin can steal the show.
    • This under-utilized fat source is uber-savory, all while boasting a moderate smoke point.
    • In a recent development, it's a technique compatible with many poultry cuts.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Top-notch crispy chicken skin can steal the show. Sure, flavorful and juicy meat is tasty, but encased in a mouth-watering crispiness, the poultry experience only gets better. Achieving such a crackly bite entails light seasoning, low moisture, and – especially crucially – a good dose of rendered fat. Cooks often use butter, oil, or lard to improve crisping, but for an extra-rich rendition, reach for duck fat.

    This under-utilized fat source is uber-savory, all while boasting a moderate smoke point. The ingredient comes as a firm paste at room temperature, meaning you'll need to melt the fat, then spread it onto the exterior of the chicken skin. The fat offers a two-for-one punch, adding both flavor and effectively crisping the skin as your chicken roasts.

    In a recent development, it's a technique compatible with many poultry cuts. In addition to an entire bird, you can add a touch to skin-on thighs or breasts, enhancing the dish in more subtle ways. Or dive in all the way and even fry your chicken in duck fat. In addition to chicken, you could make duck confit, cooking the protein in its own fat. Duck fat gives skin-on poultry that extra oomph, crisping up the skin to a delicious effect.

    According to recent reports, not sure what to pair with duck fat-covered chicken? The add-in meshes with various flavors. Season and bake a whole bird with salt and pepper alongside the fat, and you've already got a mouth-watering rendition as-is. The duck fat also pairs well with herbal seasonings like dried thyme and oregano, as well as a generous dose of garlic.

    Industry observers note that you could also consider then roasting the chicken on a bed of vegetables, letting the rich fat drip down and flavor alliums and root vegetables. Or cook the bird in the same vessel as potatoes, which can be tossed in more duck fat for good measure. Roast potatoes are 10 times richer with this magical fat; in combination with the crispy chicken skin, you'll get a truly decadent meal.

    Industry observers note that the abundant richness could use some bright elements to cut through the fat. Squeeze on some lemon — both during and after the cooking process — or finish with a drizzle of balsamic. A sprinkling of parsley goes a long way, as does a crisp glass of wine, making chicken skin a special occasion.

    #138955. Give Leftover Mashed Potatoes A Caramelized, Crispy Side With A British-Style Classic

    📅 25 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (576 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Foodrepublic ↗ Open Full Page

    Give Leftover Mashed Potatoes A Caramelized, Crispy Side With A British-Style Classic

    📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (576 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Foodrepublic

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that not many dishes can compete with mashed potatoes.
    • It has been revealed that mashed potatoes fried in butter are part of an English comfort-food classic called bubble and squeak.
    • According to recent reports, the potatoes need time to develop that crust.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that not many dishes can compete with mashed potatoes. Beyond being the ultimate comfort food, and dare we say, the best preparation of potatoes, it's also super budget-friendly, and any leftovers can be saved and used up later. But let's face it: Nothing beats freshly cooked mashed tots. You could pop leftovers in the microwave or oven to reheat them, but they often come out dry and lackluster. To give them a upcoming lease of life, borrow a tip from the Brits (who know a thing or two about mash) and fry them in butter instead.

    It has been revealed that mashed potatoes fried in butter are part of an English comfort-food classic called bubble and squeak. The dish is traditionally made from Sunday roast leftovers, with mash and cooked cabbage or other veg shallow-fried in butter, lard, or meat drippings until a crispy brown crust forms. That crust is what brings the leftovers back to life, so it's essential to let it form. This comes down to the Maillard reaction, which occurs when amino acids in the potatoes react with reducing sugars. For that to happen, you only need two things: heat and time.

    According to recent reports, the potatoes need time to develop that crust. If you drop them into the pan and start stirring them around, they'll warm through, but they won't form a base layer. Instead, pat the mash into an even layer in the pan and cook it undisturbed over medium heat for around five minutes, or until the underside is deeply golden. Then flip it and repeat. You'll hear it sizzle and pop as it fries, which is said to be where the name bubble and squeak originates from.

    In restaurants across the country, chefs are swapping high-end dining rooms for cozy neighborhood taverns – not to be confused with bars – serving food that's comforting, hearty, and nostalgic. Much of it looks like standard British pub grub, which makes bubble and squeak a natural fit for those looking to hop on the tavern food trend. It's a great side on its own, but with a few smart upgrades, it can easily become the main event.

    Since the dish goes so well with butter, you can push it into true gourmet territory by whipping up a compound butter. For reference, this is softened butter mixed with sweet or savory flavorings. It truly couldn't be easier to make, yet delivers a world of flavor. In a nod to the dish's Sunday roast heritage, mix butter with garlic, chives, and horseradish, with a spoonful of English mustard for good measure. When it comes to frying, many chefs also advocate for using lard over butter since the semi-solid pork fat has a higher smoke point, allowing the mash to develop a crispier crust. For the best bubble and squeak, we'd recommend using lard to fry, then melting a knob of the compound butter over the finished dish.

    Then there's what else can go into the dish. In the spirit of making use of your leftovers, toss in any spare roast meat, bacon, or sausage. Even better, cook the bacon or sausage from scratch in the pan first, remove it, add the butter, and let the potatoes soak up all that flavorful leftover fond. For a cheesy, tangy edge, mix a generous handful of grated cheddar and a spoonful of Dijon mustard into the mash before frying.

    #138953. Grab A Box Of Cake Mix To Make A British-Style Dessert In Half The Time

    📅 25 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (566 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Foodrepublic ↗ Open Full Page

    Grab A Box Of Cake Mix To Make A British-Style Dessert In Half The Time

    📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (566 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Foodrepublic

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Britain is home to some pretty controversial meals.
    • Sources indicate that unapologetically indulgent, sticky toffee pudding has earned itself a spot in the British food hall of fame.
    • Sources indicate that the shortcuts don't stop there.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Britain is home to some pretty controversial meals. There's the divisive beans on toast and the even more polarizing jellied eels. But one thing even the biggest haters can't fault Britain on is its dessert game, which is undeniably top-tier. There are countless cozy, comforting classics to choose from, like apple crumble, bread and butter pudding, and the elegant Victoria sponge. But one staple you can whip up using a boxed mix is a cake version of sticky toffee pudding.

    Sources indicate that unapologetically indulgent, sticky toffee pudding has earned itself a spot in the British food hall of fame. But making it at home isn't as simple as making your typical sponge. Traditionally, the recipe starts with soaking and blending dates. After that comes the batter, the baking, and the toffee sauce, which all add up to a good couple of hours. If you fancy a quick fix, a boxed mix — we ranked popular brands from worst to best — gets you most of the way there in a fraction of the time, since the flour, sugar, and leavening agents are already pre-measured, taking the guesswork out of getting a reliably fluffy sponge.

    Sources indicate that the shortcuts don't stop there. To get that classic date flavor without the soaking and blending, swap in store-bought date paste instead. The dates are already crushed, so the paste can be stirred straight into the batter as the ultimate natural sweetener. The one thing a mix can't cover is the toffee sauce, but that's the easiest part anyway. Butter, brown sugar (ideally muscovado), and cream only need a few minutes of simmering to thicken and turn glossy, so you can whip it up while the cake bakes.

    In a recent development, sticky toffee pudding is a contender for Britain's favorite dessert and has a famous fan in Gordon Ramsay, who often serves it at his world-famous restaurants. But it's also the subject of a long-running debate that revolves around the dates. Recipes vary on whether the dates should be blended or simply soaked and stirred in chopped. Blended, they disappear seamlessly into the sponge, whereas chopped, they make their presence known with a chewy bite.

    Industry observers note that fortunately, there's no right or wrong answer here, and if you enjoy more texture, you can swap the date paste for whole dates by pitting and roughly chopping them, soaking them in hot water (or coffee) until soft, then folding them into the batter just before it goes into the oven. The soaking softens the fruit so it turns jammy rather than leathery, and you can use some of the flavorful leftover liquid in place of part of the water the mix calls for.

    According to recent reports, over in the U.K., sticky toffee pudding is often served with a scoop of ice cream, and the flavor is almost always vanilla. It gets popped on top of the warm, freshly baked sponge, where the hot and cold contrast adds a latest layer to every bite. As it melts, it mingles with the toffee sauce to form a creamy, almost custardy pool that'll leave you licking your plate. You can experiment with other flavors, but there's no arguing that sweet, vanilla-forward ice cream is the perfect counterweight to the rich muscovado sugar and cooked-down toffee, cutting through the intensity so the pudding never turns cloying.

    #138951. Parthenon’s east pediment, ‘the most famous image of antiquity’, recreated in Frankfurt exhibition

    📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1125 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Theartnewspaper ↗ Open Full Page

    Parthenon’s east pediment, ‘the most famous image of antiquity’, recreated in Frankfurt exhibition

    📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1125 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Theartnewspaper

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Vinzenz Brinkmann’s quest to solve the mysteries of the destroyed east pediment of the Parthenon, which depicted the birth of Athena, dates back 40 years.
    • In 1986, he scaled ancient Greece’s most famous temple at night by rope to examine the base of the east pediment under special lamps that function only without ambient light, hoping to find traces left by 39 lost sculpted figures over the main gate.
    • “Nothing came of that,” states Brinkmann, who is now the head of antiquities at the Liebieghaus Sculpture Collection in Frankfurt—except, he adds, rumours about ghosts on the Acropolis that flew around Athens.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Vinzenz Brinkmann’s quest to solve the mysteries of the destroyed east pediment of the Parthenon, which depicted the birth of Athena, dates back 40 years.

    In 1986, he scaled ancient Greece’s most famous temple at night by rope to examine the base of the east pediment under special lamps that function only without ambient light, hoping to find traces left by 39 lost sculpted figures over the main gate.

    “Nothing came of that,” states Brinkmann, who is now the head of antiquities at the Liebieghaus Sculpture Collection in Frankfurt—except, he adds, rumours about ghosts on the Acropolis that flew around Athens.

    But now, Brinkmann says his team has solved a riddle akin to “putting together a jigsaw puzzle without having all the pieces”. The results of decades of research will go on show in an exhibition, Athena, the Stage is Yours: the Parthenon Puzzle, opening at the Liebieghaus on 18 November.

    In a recent development, long a flashpoint in Greek-British relations, the politics of the Parthenon surfaced in the run-up to the opening. The exhibition was to include marble fragments from both the British Museum in London and the Acropolis Museum in Athens. But, as The Art Newspaper reported last month, the Greek government withdrew its loan of nine fragments: according to Greek media reports, the request was rejected by Greece’s Central Archaeological Council on the grounds that they would be shown alongside British Museum pieces removed from the Acropolis by Lord Elgin. The Greek ministry of culture’s press office did not respond to emailed requests for comment and confirmation.

    Greece has for decades demanded the return of the Parthenon Marbles taken by Elgin, which have been housed in the British Museum since 1817. The Liebieghaus has, however, secured a rare loan of two fragments from the British Museum. After the Greek government’s withdrawal, a British Museum spokesperson confirmed that the museum “will still be loaning”.

    Industry observers note that “The cancellation of the loans from Greece does not detract from the exhibition’s concept, or its scholarly significance,” declares Elisabeth Pallentin, a spokesperson for the Liebieghaus. “The exhibition is based primarily on new findings resulting from many years of research at the Liebieghaus.”.

    In a recent development, the east pediment is probably “the most famous image of antiquity”, Brinkmann claims, with the centre of the sculpted ensemble composed of 3.5m-tall figures. The pediment was destroyed at some point between the fifth century AD and 1670—it is not known when or why, though there are plenty of theories—and 80% of it is still missing.

    The rest is in fragments in museums around the world. Until now, no one had succeeded in fully reconstructing the central figures, Brinkmann indicates. “In the last 200 years, there have been a lot of proposals, but we saw that there were always gaps.”.

    A reconstruction of the figures in the east pediment of the Parthenon (detail).

    Vinzenz Brinkmann and Ulrike Koch-Brinkmann, 2026. Liebieghaus Skulpturensammlung, Frankfurt am Main.

    Industry observers note that the most serious work on the east pediment had been undertaken more than a century ago by a British Museum curator, Arthur Hamilton Smith, Brinkmann notes. Smith partially recreated the east pediment using plaster casts from the British Museum and cooperated with colleagues in Athens to obtain more casts; his reconstruction went on display in the museum in 1908.

    “He did a fantastic job in preparing the way,” Brinkmann says. “That was our basis.”.

    Industry observers note that although the Liebieghaus team recreated these fragments using scans and a 3D printer, the majority of the pediment was still missing. A breakthrough came when the team began investigating reliefs from the lids of Roman sarcophagi, which proved the key to unlocking the mystery.

    It has been revealed that “It was really a chance discovery,” Brinkmann indicates. “During a visit to the Hermitage in St Petersburg in 2014, we noticed a figural relief on the lid of a sarcophagus that was clearly closely related to the composition of the east pediment. It refers to the few surviving figures from the corners of the pediment, such as Helios and Selene with their chariots, but also to figures that have repeatedly been proposed as having belonged to the east pediment, such as the Horae/Moirai.”.

    They discovered nine sarcophagi in total with relevant reliefs. Most were in the Vatican Museums and elsewhere in Rome. “They had been overlooked,” Brinkmann says. “But the Romans copied everything the Greeks did.”.

    Jaques Carrey, drawing of the east pediment (left-hand side), Temple of Minerva, Athens (1674).

    Bibliothèque nationale de France, ref.: FOL-FC-3.

    Sources indicate that none of these reliefs highlighted the entire east pediment ensemble; each depicted a different subset of the 39 figures. But with the aid of computer technology, the team established that the remaining fragments of the east pediment and the depictions on the reliefs were a 100% match.

    Sources indicate that the team’s research has yielded some surprises. It was not previously known, for instance, that the Dioscuri, the twin horsemen known as Castor and Pollux to the Romans, were portrayed on the pediment. The figures served as models for the giant figures on the Quirinale in Rome, which are almost identical and date from antiquity, Brinkmann claims. The twins are portrayed standing next to their bucking horses with anxious expressions, straining at the reins in an effort to control them.

    Sources indicate that this portrayal of the Dioscuri makes sense only in the context of the birth of the goddess, Brinkmann says. In mythology, Athena burst forth from her father Zeus’s forehead after he had swallowed her mother. Her birth is described in the Homeric hymns as causing Mount Olympus to shake, the earth to shriek, and the sea to swell and rage.

    It has been revealed that “The Dioscuri are heroic horsemen in mythology,” Brinkmann notes. “They don’t lose control of their horses. But the birth of Athena was a primordial cosmic event that unleashed a natural disaster. What we see are the consequences.” Other figures in the recreated ensemble are also responding to the cataclysm: Hermes, for instance, is depicted holding onto his hat.

    Brinkmann is known internationally for his research into polychromy in ancient Greek and Roman sculpture. An exhibition he curated, Gods in Color—Painted Sculpture of Classical Antiquity, has travelled the world, having been shown in several US locations, Athens, Oxford, Istanbul, the Vatican Museums and elsewhere.

    It is possible that the new Liebieghaus exhibition will travel too, Brinkmann indicates. But not, it seems, with marbles from the Athens collections, with recent developments giving little room to hope that a lasting settlement between Greece and the British Museum is on the horizon.

    • Athena, the Stage is Yours, Liebieghaus Sculpture Collection, Frankfurt, 18 November-25 July 2027.

    ⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read

    • Walk into the closest grocery store near you, ask an employee where that cool fun olive oil is, and they'll take you to a (metaphorically) glowing row of funky green squeeze bottles.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    We may receive a commission on purchases made from links.

    Walk into the closest grocery store near you, ask an employee where that cool fun olive oil is, and they'll take you to a (metaphorically) glowing row of funky green squeeze bottles. These are, of course, Graza bottles. It's the sensational olive oil brand that rode to fame on the slick, green waves of cute packaging and a quality product. Graza's oil comes primarily from Jaén, Spain. The company commits to a single origin and single varietal mission, so the oil in your newly-acquired bottle comes from a single place and a single type of olive.

    Industry observers note that you'll undoubtedly notice that Graza has some acolytes waiting on the shelves next to its empire of squeeze bottles. Whether they existed before or after Graza debuted on the scene, each of these unique oils takes after Graza in some way; some are also from Andalusia, while others sport a youthful aesthetic. If you're interested in what's beyond Graza olive oil, we think these alternatives are totally worth trying out.

    Hopping onto the green squeeze-bottle trend is O Olive Oil and Vinegar's organic California Extra Virgin Olive Oil. Though do note that the olive oil also comes in glass bottle form, so there's a version for everyone's packaging preferences. Olive oil-heads will enjoy the fruity notes in this oil that evoke Graza's Sizzle product. Squeeze it into a hot pan for a delicately sweet cooking oil, or combine with any of O's extensive line of vinegars in a dressing or marinade so good you'll want to drink it.

    These bottles proudly wear that tantalizing "first cold pressed" label that tingles our wallets, which is the first signal that you're looking at a quality olive oil. Though all extra virgin olive oils are cold pressed and kept below 80 F, first cold pressed means that the olives were only crushed (or processed) once, making for a richer oil with more nutrients. Besides the label, O California Extra Virgin Olive Oil has a really pleasant flavor that'll be a talented supporting player in your culinary ensemble.

    In a recent development, A Greek olive oil whose name screams professional, The Chef's Way oil by Iliada is in a squeeze bottle to provide convenient flavor whenever you need it. The Chef's Way is single-variety and pulsing with Mediterranean flavor like almonds and artichokes, which breaks up your regularly scheduled olive oil programming with a nicely acidic interlude.

    It has been revealed that it may be scary for the olive oil purists to be accosted by an aisle of squeeze bottles when you walk into the store nowadays. But one easy, squeezy afternoon of cooking will change their minds completely with the undeniable convenience. The Chef's Way olive oil comes in several different flavors, including Kalamata PDO Extra Virgin and Premium Greek Extra Virgin, so you can choose whichever variation calls to you the most. Put on your chef whites, nonslip shoes, and backwards hat, because The Chef's Way is coming to transform your home kitchen into one of those casually elegant eateries.

    It has been revealed that costco lovers, you're going to appreciate this find. The Kirkland-branded olive oil warrants its own inclusion in this article because of its robust flavor and versatility. Like Graza, Kirkland's best olive oil comes from Spain, the country that beats Italy as the top olive oil producer in the world.

    The Kirkland Signature Spanish Extra Virgin Olive Oil comes in an absurdly large jug, like many other items at Costco, so you'll get an incredible value for your money. It's the perfect olive oil to use in baking to add a strong, but not abrasive, creaminess. For instance, an olive oil cakes would be the perfect vehicle for the Kirkland Signature Spanish Extra Virgin Olive Oil. Olive oil cake batters tend to eat up a cup or more of oil, which can get really expensive really fast. You can save your fancy olive oil for other pursuits. But don't worry — this olive oil isn't only suited for baking. It can accommodate your shallow frying and vinaigrette needs, as well.

    Another Spanish olive oil from Jaén, Oro Bailén has that slick aesthetic appeal of Graza, along with the high-quality taste. While it can be a little pricier than Graza, it offers something Graza does not: A slightly more acidic olive oil for those times when you want a punchier flavor. The brand offers a few different intensities, so you can choose how much punch you want in your olive oil. Along with the punch, you'll find notes of banana that add a ripeness you don't encounter so often with run-of-the-mill olive oils.

    Oro Bailén oils comes from Picual olives, harvested very early and milled very swiftly to obtain what it instead calls "olive juice," bringing to mind a flavorful and nourishing elixir you'll want to have in your kitchen. Oro Bailén has a forward quality in its flavor: outgoing, fruity, and spicy. Like Graza, which also sells potato chips, Oro Bailén has some intriguing offshoot products, like EVOO pearls and an olive oil jam for when a simple oil isn't enough to put on bread.

    Featuring sleek labeling that tells you everything you need to know about the brand, Brightland Extra Virgin Olive Oil belongs to the same cool kids club that Graza is currently the ringleader of. Brightland's product line also closely resembles Graza's, offering several different types of oils for different purposes, including a popular pizza oil (which is different from olive oil). Brightland is the kind of olive oil you'll want to casually leave out on your dinner table to impress your guests.

    High in polyphenols, which have healthy antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties, Brightland feels as attractively carefree as it looks. The brand has also branched out into different varieties and flavors of oil, as mentioned above, in a manner more abstract and artsy than Graza. "Lucid," "Rosette," and "Arise" are some of the olive oil options when it comes to Brightland, signifying lemon, garlic, and basil. These options give you the same carefree star power you can feel when putting down a bottle of Graza on your table.

    If Martha Stewart tells you to get some olive oil, you can expect two things: It'll be wicked expensive, and likely delicious. Flamingo Estate's olive oil line is perhaps a more luxurious option than Graza's, but it has a peppery bite thanks to the quick processing that will be reminiscent of Graza's "drizzle" finishing oil. Martha Stewart swears by this $50 bottle, the olives of which come from Ojai, California.

    Recent findings suggest that this oil is green, sumptuous, and glossy — you'll want to dip a finger into it. Though it is cosmically destined for a hunk of crusty bread, Flamingo Estate's oil also has a high smoke point, so you can use this verdant gold in the oven or on the stovetop. The look of it is one of its best qualities, so a fresh drizzle will be a beautiful finish to your dishes. It isn't unlike Martha, when you think about it: It's vibrant, tasteful, and one of the fanciest things you could come across in your kitchen.

    In a recent development, kosterina is an award-winning Greek olive oil, and right away you can tell: Its shiny white bottle looks like it was plucked right from the Mediterranean. The olives for this brand are harvested early, so the resulting olive oil is a little more assertive than Graza's Sizzle, but it's just as versatile. This is a single varietal olive oil, made from only Koroneiki olives that are nutrient- and oil-rich. Single varietal oils can have a crisper flavor compared to blends, and Kosterina is as refined as they come.

    Buying a metal bottle of Kosterina olive oil — metal, as it helps prevent oxidation and harmful chemicals leaching into the oil from plastic — feels intentional in a similar way to getting one from Graza. It feels a little better for the environment, and it even tastes like it's doing you good. Another way that Graza's changed the home-cooking game: No longer can a home kitchen function with one singular olive oil. Now, you need one for cooking and another one for drizzling. Kosterina follows suit with this idea, offering even more choices for your olive oil-purchasing escapades.
